components/project-management/README.title: README
components/project-management/README.content:
Project Management App
Unified personal project and task management using an Areas → Projects → Tasks → Backlog hierarchy, inspired by Things 3 and the PARA method.
Purpose
The Project Management app provides structured organization for work and life responsibilities across four levels:

Areas - Ongoing life categories (Work, Health, Learning) that don’t have end dates
Projects - Goal-oriented containers with defined outcomes and optional deadlines
Tasks - Actionable work items that move projects forward
Backlog - Quick-capture system for ideas and reminders to prevent distraction

This creates a clear hierarchy: Life Areas contain Projects, which contain Tasks, fed by the Backlog capture system.
Quick Start
Create a Task
Use natural language during any session:
create task to design homepage mockup for Website Redesign project due Friday p1

Claude will:

Generate a ULID for the task
Create file: task-YYYYMMDD-NNN.md
Link to the specified project
Set due date and priority
Confirm creation

Create a Project
create project Website Redesign in Work area deadline March 1

View Your Tasks
Open components/project-management/project-management-dashboard.md for:

Today’s tasks (scheduled or due today)
Active projects overview
Areas at a glance

Core Concepts
Areas
Areas are the major categories of your life that require continuous attention. Unlike projects, they don’t have end dates—they represent ongoing responsibilities.
Default Areas:













































AreaIconPurposeWork💼Professional responsibilities, careerPersonal🏠Home, admin, life managementHealth & Fitness💪Exercise, nutrition, wellnessLearning📚Education, skill developmentFamily & Friends👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Relationships, social connectionsFinance💰Money, investments, budgetingCreative🎨Art, writing, hobbies
Projects
Projects are goal-oriented work with a defined outcome. They optionally have deadlines and always belong to an Area.
Project characteristics:

Has a clear definition of “done” (outcome)
Contains multiple related tasks
May have a deadline
Belongs to one Area
Has a status: not-started, active, completed, on-hold, cancelled

Tasks
Tasks are the atomic unit of work—specific, actionable items you can complete.
Two key date fields (inspired by Things 3):

when - Flexible intention: when you PLAN to work on this
deadline - Fixed obligation: when this MUST be done

This separation lets you schedule tasks for specific days without creating false urgency.
When vs Deadline: Deep Dive
One of Things 3’s most powerful design decisions is the separation between when (plan) and deadline (obligation). Understanding this distinction is crucial for stress-free task management.
When (Flexible Intention)

Purpose: “I plan to work on this today”
Feeling: Low pressure, flexible
Psychology: Positive intention, not a commitment
Typical use: Daily planning, time blocking
Behavior: Can be rescheduled guilt-free
Visibility: Shows in Today view, helps focus your day

Deadline (Fixed Obligation)

Purpose: “This must be done by this date”
Feeling: High pressure, urgent as it approaches
Psychology: External commitment, real consequences
Typical use: Client deliverables, bills, appointments
Behavior: Rescheduling requires negotiation/consequences
Visibility: Shows urgency indicators as date approaches

Best Practices:


Use deadlines sparingly - Only for true hard deadlines

✅ Client project due Friday
✅ Pay rent by 1st of month
✅ File taxes by April 15
❌ “Finish reading book” (no external pressure)
❌ “Clean garage” (flexible goal)



Use when liberally - For daily planning and intentions

✅ Schedule “Write blog post” for Wednesday
✅ Block Thursday morning for “Review quarterly goals”
✅ Plan “Call mom” for weekend



Combine both for buffer time

Task: Prepare presentation
when: Wednesday (work on it)
deadline: Friday (must be done)
Result: 2-day buffer if something goes wrong



Inbox tasks have neither - Uncategorized, not scheduled

Captured ideas waiting to be organized
Will be scheduled during weekly review



Examples:









































TaskwhendeadlineReasoningSubmit expense reportWedFriWork on Wednesday, due Friday (buffer)Daily standup9am daily—Recurring intention, not a deadlineClient deliverable—Mar 15True deadline, plan work separatelyWrite blog postMon—Personal goal, flexible timingPay credit card—1stHard deadline, do anytime before
Common Patterns:

when only: Personal goals, flexible work
deadline only: Bills, appointments (do anytime before)
Both: Important deliverables with buffer time
Neither: Inbox tasks, someday/maybe items

Backlog
The Backlog is a quick-capture system for ideas, tasks, and reminders that prevents distraction from current work. It’s the entry point for the entire system—ideas flow from Backlog → Tasks → Projects.
Backlog characteristics:

Quick capture with natural language
Minimal friction (no ceremony, AI handles details)
Triage weekly during reviews
Promote to Tasks when ready to execute
Cancel ruthlessly if no longer relevant

Key properties:

status: open, completed, canceled, someday
priority: p0-p3 for triage
category: Life area classification
estimate: Time/effort estimation
context: Why/where this came up

Workflow:

Capture - Create backlog item during any session
Triage - Weekly review, update priorities
Promote - Move to Tasks when committed to work
Complete - Mark done or cancel if no longer needed

For detailed documentation, see the Backlog section below.
File Structure
components/project-management/
├── README.md                         # This file
├── project-management-dashboard.md   # Landing page
├── manifest.json
├── areas-base.base                   # Areas view
├── backlog-base.base                 # Backlog items (4 views)
├── projects-base.base                # Projects (4 views)
├── tasks-base.base                   # Tasks (8 views)
└── today-base.base                   # Today's tasks

_database/database-core/               # Data tables
├── areas-table/
├── projects-table/
├── tasks-table/
└── backlog-table/

Property Schemas
Area Properties
# Required
uid: 01KCPM001WORK00000000000000
date: 2025-12-17
user: tomboo
type: area
title: Work
 
# Standard
status: active              # active, paused, archived
icon: 💼                    # Emoji for visual ID
sort-order: 1               # Display order
tags: [area]
created-at: 2025-12-17T10:00:00-08:00
 
# Optional
description: Professional work and career development
Project Properties
# Required
uid: 01KCPM002PROJ00000000000000
date: 2025-12-17
user: tomboo
type: project
title: Website Redesign
 
# Standard
status: active              # not-started, active, completed, on-hold, cancelled
priority: p1                # p0-p3
area: "[[../areas-table/area-work]]"
tags: [project]
created-at: 2025-12-17T10:00:00-08:00
 
# Optional
description: Redesign personal website
outcome: Live website with new design and portfolio
deadline: 2025-03-01
Task Properties
# Required
uid: 01KCPM003TASK00000000000000
date: 2025-12-17
user: tomboo
type: task
title: Design homepage mockup
 
# Standard
status: not-started         # not-started, in-progress, completed, blocked, cancelled
priority: p2                # p0-p3
project: "[[../projects-table/project-20251217-001]]"
tags: [task]
created-at: 2025-12-17T10:00:00-08:00
 
# Scheduling
when: 2025-12-18            # When you plan to work on it
deadline: 2025-12-20        # Hard deadline (must be done)
 
# Optional
area: "[[../areas-table/area-work]]"  # Direct area (if no project)
estimate: PT2H              # Time estimate (ISO 8601)
context: Additional notes
Natural Language Workflow
Creating Tasks
Basic task:
create task to review quarterly budget

With project:
create task to design logo for Website Redesign project

With scheduling:
create task to call dentist tomorrow
  → Sets when: tomorrow (flexible plan)

create task to prepare presentation due Friday scheduled Wednesday
  → Sets when: Wednesday, deadline: Friday (buffer time)

create task to pay rent deadline Dec 1
  → Sets deadline: Dec 1 only (do anytime before)

With priority:
create task to fix critical bug p0
create task to update documentation p3

With estimate:
create task to write blog post 2h
create task to send email 15m

Full example:
create task to design homepage mockup for Website Redesign due Dec 20 scheduled tomorrow p1 2h

Creating Projects
create project Learn Python Basics in Learning area deadline March 2026
create project Bathroom Renovation in Personal area p1

Updating Tasks
mark task-001 as completed
set task-002 to in-progress
reschedule task-003 to Monday
change task-004 priority to p1

Quick Queries
show tasks due today
show tasks for Website Redesign project
show all p0 and p1 tasks
show tasks in Work area

Views
The Project Management app provides multiple views optimized for different workflows, inspired by Things 3’s organization philosophy.
Task Views
Access via components/project-management/tasks-base.base:
1. Inbox
Purpose: Uncategorized tasks waiting to be organized
Shows:

All open tasks (status = open)
No when date
No deadline
No project assigned

Workflow:

New tasks land here by default
During daily/weekly review, organize them:

Assign to project or area
Set when or deadline if time-sensitive
Cancel if no longer relevant


Goal: Keep inbox at zero

Best for: Quick capture, weekly review
2. Today
Purpose: What to work on today
Shows:

Tasks with when = today (planned for today)
Tasks with deadline = today (due today)
Overdue tasks (deadline < today)
Status = open

Sorted by: Priority, then deadline
Workflow:

Review each morning
Reschedule tasks that won’t get done (guilt-free!)
Focus on completing this list

Best for: Daily execution, morning planning
3. Upcoming
Purpose: Next 7 days preview
Shows:

Tasks with when in next 7 days
Tasks with deadline in next 7 days
Status = open

Sorted by: Deadline, then priority
Workflow:

Weekly planning sessions
Identify conflicts and capacity issues
Reschedule overcommitted days

Best for: Weekly planning, capacity management
4. Someday
Purpose: Tasks without specific timeframes
Shows:

No when date
No deadline
Has project or area assigned (organized, unlike Inbox)
Status = open

Grouped by: Project/Area
Workflow:

Passive backlog of organized but unscheduled work
Pull from here during weekly review
Schedule when ready to commit

Best for: Long-term project tasks, “when I have time” items
5. Anytime (By Project)
Purpose: All open tasks organized by project
Shows:

Status = open
Grouped by project

Sorted by: Priority within each project
Best for: Project-focused work sessions, understanding project scope
6. Anytime (By Area)
Purpose: All open tasks organized by life area
Shows:

Status = open
Grouped by area

Sorted by: Priority within each area
Best for: Area-focused reviews (e.g., “Health week”, “Work sprint”)
7. Logbook
Purpose: Completed and canceled task history
Shows:

Status = completed or canceled
Includes completed-at or canceled-at timestamps

Sorted by: Completion date (newest first)
Best for: Progress tracking, weekly review retrospectives, accountability
8. All Tasks
Purpose: Complete task database
Shows: Every task regardless of status
Columns: Title, Status, Priority, Project, When, Deadline
Best for: Searching, data analysis, troubleshooting
Project Views
Access via components/project-management/projects-base.base:
All Projects: Complete project list with status, area, deadline
Active Projects: Only status = open projects
Logbook: Completed/canceled projects with completion dates
Area Views
Access via components/project-management/areas-base.base:
All Areas: Complete area list with project count, task count
Today View (Standalone)
Access via components/project-management/today-base.base:
Dedicated single-view file for embedding in daily notes or dashboard. Identical to the Today view in tasks-base.base.
Backlog Views
Access via components/project-management/backlog-base.base:
All Items: Complete backlog
Open Items: Active backlog items
By Priority: Grouped by p0/p1/p2/p3
Quick Wins: Short tasks (< 30m) with high priority
Recurring Tasks
The Project Management app supports recurring tasks through the repeat property, inspired by Things 3’s flexible recurrence model.
Property: repeat (String)
Pattern Types
1. Fixed Schedule (repeats on calendar intervals)
Perfect for tasks that happen on a regular schedule regardless of when you complete them:
repeat: daily            # Every day
repeat: weekly           # Every week (same day of week)
repeat: monthly          # Every month (same day of month)
repeat: yearly           # Every year (same date)
repeat: weekdays         # Monday-Friday only
repeat: weekends         # Saturday-Sunday only
repeat: every-3-days     # Custom day interval
repeat: every-2-weeks    # Custom week interval
repeat: every-3-months   # Custom month interval
2. After Completion (repeats N time after completing)
Perfect for maintenance tasks where timing starts after completion:
repeat: daily-after-completion         # 1 day after completing
repeat: weekly-after-completion        # 1 week after completing
repeat: monthly-after-completion       # 1 month after completing
repeat: yearly-after-completion        # 1 year after completing
repeat: 3-days-after-completion        # Custom days
repeat: 2-weeks-after-completion       # Custom weeks
repeat: 6-months-after-completion      # Custom months
When to Use Each Type
Fixed Schedule:

Team meetings (every Monday)
Daily habits (meditation, exercise)
Bills and deadlines (1st of month)
Regular reviews (weekly, monthly)
Example: Weekly standup always happens Monday 9am, regardless of when you mark it complete

After Completion:

Home maintenance (change air filter every 3 months after changing)
Health tasks (dental checkup 6 months after last visit)
Flexible maintenance (water plants 3 days after last watering)
Example: Change air filter completed Jan 15 → next instance scheduled Apr 15

Complete Examples
Fixed Schedule: Team Standup
uid: 01XXXXX
title: Team standup
repeat: weekly
when: 2025-12-30T09:00:00-08:00  # Monday 9am
project: "[[../projects-table/project-work-team]]"
tags: [work, meeting, recurring]
Completes Friday → next instance still Monday 9am
After Completion: Change Air Filter
uid: 01YYYYY
title: Change HVAC air filter
repeat: 3-months-after-completion
when: 2025-12-25
area: "[[../areas-table/area-home]]"
estimate: PT30M
tags: [home, maintenance, recurring]
Completes Jan 15 → next instance scheduled Apr 15
Weekdays: Review Emails
uid: 01ZZZZZ
title: Review and respond to emails
repeat: weekdays
when: 2025-12-23T08:00:00-08:00  # Monday 8am
area: "[[../areas-table/area-work]]"
estimate: PT30M
tags: [work, communication, recurring]
Repeats Monday-Friday only, skips weekends
Workflow

Create recurring task with repeat property
Complete the task (mark status = completed)
System auto-creates next instance:

Fixed schedule: Increments from original date
After completion: Increments from completion date


Original task preserved with completed-at timestamp in Logbook

Best Practices
Choose the right pattern:

Use fixed schedule for time-sensitive commitments
Use after-completion for flexible maintenance tasks
Use weekdays for work-only tasks
Use custom intervals for non-standard schedules

Keep titles consistent:

Same title helps track history in Logbook
Use tags to distinguish instances if needed

Date field guidance:

Use when for most recurring tasks (flexible)
Use deadline only for recurring obligations (bills, reports)
Combine both if task has fixed deadline but flexible work time

Don’t over-use:

Only create recurring tasks for true patterns
One-off tasks should not have repeat
Review recurring tasks quarterly - cancel outdated ones

Implementation Status

✅ Basic patterns (daily, weekly, monthly, yearly)
🚧 After-completion patterns (schema defined, implementation pending)
🚧 Complex patterns (weekdays, every-N-days) (schema defined, implementation pending)

See standards/schemas/app-schemas.md#repeat for complete technical specification.
See Also:

Task-070: Enhanced repeat property schema (Phase 2 - complete)
Things 3 philosophy guide (task-072) for recurrence philosophy

Workflows
Daily Planning

Open Today view each morning
Review scheduled and due tasks
Reschedule tasks that won’t get done
Add any new tasks that came up
Work through Today list

Weekly Review

Review all active projects
Check for stalled projects (no recent task activity)
Process completed tasks
Schedule tasks for the upcoming week
Review areas for balance

Creating from Backlog
Promote backlog items to tasks when ready to execute:
promote backlog-20251217-001 to task in Website Redesign project

This creates a task linked to the original backlog item.
Best Practices
Task Naming
Use action verbs:

✅ “Design homepage mockup”
✅ “Review budget spreadsheet”
✅ “Call dentist to schedule appointment”
❌ “Homepage” (not actionable)
❌ “Budget stuff” (vague)

Schedule Strategically
Use when and deadline together for important work with buffer time:

deadline: External deadlines, commitments to others
when: When YOU plan to work on it

Example: A report due Friday might be scheduled (when) for Wednesday, giving buffer time.
See the When vs Deadline: Deep Dive section for comprehensive guidance.
Keep Areas Stable
Areas should be relatively stable life categories. If you’re creating/deleting areas frequently, they might be better as projects.
Project Outcomes
Always define what “done” looks like:

✅ “Live website with new design and portfolio”
❌ “Work on website” (never ends)

Limit Active Projects
Per PARA method guidance, keep 10-15 active projects maximum. More than that indicates:

Some projects should be on-hold
Some “projects” are actually areas
Scope creep

Integration with Other Apps
Backlog App

Backlog: Quick capture, ideas, someday/maybe
Project Management: Committed work with scheduling

Workflow: Capture in Backlog → Triage weekly → Promote to Tasks
Sessions App

Link sessions to projects/tasks worked on
Session notes reference completed tasks
Track progress over time

Daily Notes

Embed Today view in daily note
Quick task creation from daily note context

Troubleshooting
Task not showing in Today view
Check:

Is when or deadline set to today?
Is status set to open (not completed or canceled)?
Is the file in _database/database-core/tasks-table/?

Project has no tasks
Either:

Tasks exist but aren’t linked (check project property)
Project is newly created and needs tasks added

Area seems empty

Check if projects are linked to the area
Ensure projects have area property set correctly

Backlog App Details
Quick Capture Workflow
Create backlog items with natural language during any session:
create backlog item to research Obsidian plugin API
create p1 backlog item to fix critical bug
create backlog item for health-fitness to schedule checkup estimate 30m

What AI does automatically:

Generates ULID for unique identification
Creates file: _database/database-core/backlog-table/backlog-NNN.md
Parses priority, category, estimate from natural language
Sets defaults (priority: p2, status: open)
Confirms creation

Backlog Properties
Required:

uid - ULID identifier
date - Creation date
user - Creator
title - Brief description

Standard:

status - open | completed | canceled | someday
priority - p0 (critical) | p1 (high) | p2 (medium) | p3 (low)
category - Life area (health-fitness, learning, work-projects, etc.)
tags - Categorization
created-at - Timestamps

Optional:

estimate - Time estimate (30m, 2h, 3d)
context - Why/where this came up
deadline - Due date if time-sensitive
related-to - Links to sessions/projects
github-issue - GitHub issue number if promoted

Triage Strategies
Weekly Review:

Open backlog views in components/project-management/backlog-base.base
Sort by priority and date
Review open items
Update priorities based on current goals
Cancel items no longer relevant

Quick Wins:
Filter for:

estimate: 30m or less
priority: p0, p1, or p2
status: open

Perfect for short productive breaks.
Category Focus:

Health week: category: health-fitness
Learning sprint: category: learning
Home maintenance: category: home-maintenance

Promoting to Tasks
When ready to commit to work on a backlog item:
promote backlog-001 to task in Website Redesign project

This creates a task linked to the backlog item, moving it from “someday” to “committed.”
Best Practices
Capture Immediately:

Don’t let ideas interrupt current work
Use natural language, no ceremony
AI handles all details

Add Context:

Include why/where idea came up
Link to related sessions
Future you will thank you

Be Ruthless:

Cancel items that no longer matter
Don’t let backlog become overwhelming
Delete completed items if no history value

Review Regularly:

Weekly triage keeps backlog healthy
Update priorities as life changes
Celebrate completed items

Related Documentation

standards/schemas/app-schemas.md#project-management-app - Full schema
standards/schemas/common-properties.md - Shared properties
standards/development.md - Development standards
PRD.md - Product requirements and roadmap

Version History

components/sessions/README.title: README
components/sessions/README.content:
Sessions App
Track work sessions with Claude Code, capture progress, and maintain comprehensive session history.
Purpose
The Sessions app provides structured workflows for beginning, working through, and concluding collaborative sessions with Claude Code. It ensures:

Continuity: Each session starts with context from previous work
Documentation: Comprehensive notes capture what was accomplished
Git Integration: Automated, well-formatted commits at checkpoints and session end
Focus: Clear goals and accountability for each session
Health Monitoring: AI validates schema compliance and framework health

Quick Start
Start a Session
/session-start

This will:

Sync with remote (git pull)
Review recent commits and last session notes
Check recent vault modifications
Display context usage
Ask what you want to focus on

During a Session
Work naturally with Claude Code. Every 15-30 minutes:
/session-commit

This creates checkpoint commits (local only, no push).
End a Session
/session-end

This will:

Create comprehensive session note
Auto-generate commit message
Run health checks
Display context usage
Ask for commit confirmation
Optionally push to remote

File Structure
Location
All session files are stored in planning/sessions/.
Naming Convention
Pattern: session-YYYYMMDD-NNN.md
Examples:

session-20251213-001.md - First session on Dec 13, 2025
session-20251213-002.md - Second session on same day
session-20251214-001.md - First session on Dec 14, 2025

Components:

session- prefix
Date: YYYYMMDD (compact, sortable)
Session number: NNN (zero-padded, 001-999)

Bases View
Use _index.base to view and filter sessions in Obsidian.
Property Schema
Required Properties
uid: 01KAGWC2WNMNDGH2PP6NYZY8BY  # ULID, auto-generated
date: 2025-12-13                  # Session date
session: 1                        # Session number for this date
user: tomboo                      # Session owner
focus: [organization, planning]   # Focus areas (list)
Standard Properties
tags: [framework, session]        # Categorization
created-at: 2025-12-13T14:30:00-08:00
duration-estimate: ~2h            # Planned duration
Optional Properties
actual-duration: 2h15m            # Actual time spent
context-usage: 45K/200K           # Context at session end
commits: [d86a850, eeb43f0]       # Git commits from session
related-backlog: [[backlog-001]]  # Backlog items addressed
Property Details
uid

Type: String (ULID)
Auto-generated: Yes (by AI)
Format: 26-character Base32 encoded
Example: 01KAGWC2WNMNDGH2PP6NYZY8BY
Purpose: Unique identifier for cross-referencing

date

Type: Date
Format: YYYY-MM-DD
Example: 2025-12-13
Purpose: Primary date of session

session

Type: Number
Format: Positive integer (1, 2, 3…)
Purpose: Distinguish multiple sessions on same day
Usage: Combined with date for filename

user

Type: String
Default: tomboo
Purpose: Session owner/creator

focus

Type: List of Strings
Format: kebab-case values
Required: At least one focus area
Common values:

writing - Content creation, documentation
organization - Vault structure, file management
projects - Specific project work
research - Information gathering
review - Editing, refactoring
planning - Strategic planning
learning - Skill development
health-fitness - Exercise, nutrition tracking



duration-estimate

Type: String
Format: ~Xh, ~Xm, or ~XhYm
Examples: ~2h, ~45m, ~1h30m
Purpose: Planned session length
Tilde (~): Indicates estimate

actual-duration

Type: String
Format: Xh, Xm, or XhYm (no tilde)
Example: 2h15m
Purpose: Track actual time spent
Usage: Compare estimates vs. actuals

Session Note Structure
Created automatically by /session-end:
---
uid: 01KAGWC2WNMNDGH2PP6NYZY8BY
date: 2025-12-13
session: 1
user: tomboo
focus: [organization, planning]
duration-estimate: ~2h
actual-duration: 2h15m
tags: [framework, session]
created-at: 2025-12-13T14:30:00-08:00
context-usage: 45K/200K
---
 
# Session 20251213-001: Framework Planning
 
**User:** tomboo
**Focus:** Organization / Planning
 
## Summary
 
2-3 sentence summary of what was accomplished.
 
## Content Created
 
**Planning:**
- Item 1
- Item 2
 
**Concepts Developed:**
- Concept 1
- Concept 2
 
## Organization Work
 
**Changes to structure:**
- Change 1
- Change 2
 
**Key Decisions:**
- Decision 1
- Decision 2
 
## Research Completed
 
**Topics Explored:**
- Topic 1
- Topic 2
 
**Conclusions:**
- Finding 1
- Finding 2
 
## Files Created/Modified
 
**Created:**
- File 1
- File 2
 
**Modified:**
- File 3
- File 4
 
## Next Steps
 
**Immediate (Next Session):**
- [ ] Task 1
- [ ] Task 2
 
**Future:**
- [ ] Task 3
- [ ] Task 4
 
## Notes
 
### [Section Title]
 
Additional context, insights, or important information.
Slash Commands
/session-start
Purpose: Begin a new working session
What it does:

Checks git status

Stops if uncommitted tracked changes exist
Automatically runs git pull if clean


Reviews recent commits (last 5)
Checks git user identity
Reads most recent session note
Lists recently modified files
Displays context usage
Asks for session focus

Output includes:

Recent commits summary
Last session summary
Recent vault modifications
Context status
Prompt for focus area

When to use: At the start of every work session
/session-commit
Purpose: Create checkpoint commits during active work
What it does:

Analyzes changed files
Categorizes changes (content, organization, config)
Generates descriptive commit message
Creates LOCAL commit (no push)
Displays commit summary

When to use: Every 15-30 minutes during active sessions
Note: Commits are local only. Use /session-end to optionally push.
/session-end
Purpose: Conclude a working session with comprehensive tracking
What it does:

Creates detailed session note in planning/sessions/
Auto-generates commit message from session work
Runs health checks on modified files
Displays context usage
Asks for commit confirmation
Offers push to remote (optional)

Output includes:

Session note with full structure
Health check results
Context status
Commit preview

When to use: At the end of every work session
Workflow Examples
Typical Session Flow
# Start session
/session-start
# → Reviews last session, shows context
# → User selects focus: "Organization"
 
# Work for 30 minutes...
 
# Checkpoint commit
/session-commit
# → "Auto-commit: Update framework documentation"
 
# Work for another hour...
 
# End session
/session-end
# → Creates session-20251213-001.md
# → "Session 2025-12-13-1: Framework Planning"
# → Confirms commit, optionally pushes
Multiple Sessions in One Day
# Morning session
/session-start
# ...work...
/session-end
# → Creates session-20251213-001.md
 
# Afternoon session
/session-start
# ...work...
/session-end
# → Creates session-20251213-002.md
Session with Health Issues
/session-end
# → Health Check: ⚠ Issues found
# → backlog/item-001.md: Missing uid property
# → Would you like me to fix these automatically?
# → User: Yes
# → ✓ Fixed, session committed
Health Monitoring
AI validates at session boundaries:
Schema Compliance

All session files have required properties
Properties follow correct formats
UIDs are valid ULIDs
Dates are valid ISO 8601

Naming Conventions

Files follow session-YYYYMMDD-NNN.md pattern
Properties use kebab-case
Values use kebab-case

Data Integrity

UIDs are unique across vault
No duplicate session numbers for same date
All references resolve correctly

Auto-Fix Capability
With user confirmation, AI can:

Add missing properties
Fix format violations
Generate missing UIDs
Rename files to conventions

Context Management
Display Format
All session commands show:
Context: 39K/200K (19% used, 161K remaining) ✓

Warning Levels

GREEN (0-50%): ✓ Healthy
YELLOW (51-75%): ⚠ Monitor
RED (76-90%): 🔴 Consider snapshot
CRITICAL (91-100%): 🚨 Consolidation recommended

Manual Consolidation
Use /session-snapshot when:

Context approaching 75%+
Before complex multi-file refactoring
When context feels “bloated”
At end of major work phases

Migration from Old Format
If you have existing session files in old format:
Old format:
planning/sessions/2025-12-13-session-1-framework-planning.md

New format:
planning/sessions/session-20251213-001.md

Migration adds:

ULID in frontmatter
Kebab-case properties
Consistent filename pattern
Timestamps (created-at)

See migration plan in Phase 2 implementation.
Best Practices
Consistent Usage

Always start with /session-start
Use /session-commit every 15-30 minutes
Always end with /session-end

Focus Definition

Be specific with focus areas
Use 1-3 focus values (don’t over-categorize)
Combine related work under single focus

Duration Estimates

Be realistic with estimates
Track actuals to improve future estimates
Consider breaks in longer sessions

Session Notes

Let AI generate the structure
Add your own notes in the Notes section
Use Next Steps for clear follow-up

Git Hygiene

Checkpoint commits keep work safe
Session-end commits are comprehensive
Push to remote at logical breakpoints

Troubleshooting
Session number not incrementing

Check existing session files for today’s date
Verify numbering is sequential (001, 002, 003)
AI should auto-detect and use next number

Health checks failing

Review error messages from /session-end
Use auto-fix if offered
Manually fix in Obsidian if needed

Context usage high

Use /session-snapshot to consolidate
Consider ending session and starting fresh
Review what’s consuming context

Git conflicts on pull

/session-start will warn if uncommitted changes
Commit or stash changes before starting session
Resolve conflicts manually if needed

Related Documentation

standards/schemas/common-properties.md - Shared properties
standards/development.md - Development standards
standards/ai-guidelines.md - AI interaction standards
APPS.md - App registry

Version History

TableCountDescriptionbeats-table33Story beats with act, sequence, scene infocharacters-table38Character profiles with tier, relationshipslocations-table51Location reference with hierarchy

Beat Properties

what-happens, reader-now-knows, still-hidden

components/subscriptions/README.title: README
components/subscriptions/README.content:
Subscriptions App
Track recurring payments with cost visibility, renewal reminders, and audit trail.
Purpose
The Subscriptions app provides centralized tracking of all recurring payments and subscriptions. It helps you:

See total spend across all subscriptions (monthly/yearly)
Get renewal reminders before charges hit
Audit your subscriptions to spot waste and forgotten services
Track history of what you’ve subscribed to over time

Quick Start
Creating a subscription
Ask Claude to create a subscription using natural language:
create subscription Netflix $15.99/month entertainment renews on the 15th
create subscription Spotify $9.99/month music yearly billing
create subscription Claude Pro $20/month software @work

Viewing subscriptions
Open components/subscriptions/subscriptions-base.base in Obsidian to see:

All Subscriptions
Active Only (grouped by category)
By Category (for spend analysis)
Upcoming Renewals (next 30 days)
Cancelled (archive)

File Structure
components/subscriptions/
├── README.md                         # This file
├── subscriptions-dashboard.md        # Landing page
├── subscriptions-base.base           # Bases view
└── manifest.json

_database/database-core/subscriptions-table/         # Subscription data files

File Naming
Subscription files follow sequential naming convention:
subscription-NNN.md

Examples:

subscription-001.md (first subscription)
subscription-002.md (second subscription)
subscription-050.md (fiftieth subscription)

Sequential numbering provides stable, short references for long-lived subscription data.
Property Schema
Required Properties









































PropertyTypeFormatDescriptionuidstringULIDUnique identifier, auto-generateddatedateYYYY-MM-DDCreation dateuserstring-Owner (tomboo)typestring-Always “subscription”titlestring-Service name (e.g., “Netflix”)
Standard Properties





























PropertyTypeFormatDescriptionstatusenum-active, paused, cancelled, trialtagslistkebab-caseCategorization tagscreated-atdatetimeISO 8601When item was created
Subscription-Specific Properties



















































































PropertyTypeFormatDescriptionamountnumberdecimalCost per billing cycle (e.g., 15.99)currencystringISO 4217Currency code (default: USD)frequencyenum-weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearlybilling-daynumber1-31Day of period when billednext-billingdateYYYY-MM-DDNext charge datecategoryenum-See categories belowpayment-methodstring-Card/account identifier (e.g., “visa-1234”)auto-renewboolean-Whether it auto-renewscancellation-urlstringURLDirect link to cancelproviderstring-Company namestarted-atdateYYYY-MM-DDWhen subscription begancancelled-atdateYYYY-MM-DDWhen cancelled (if applicable)
Categories

entertainment - Streaming, games, media
software - Apps, tools, SaaS
services - Professional services
news - Publications, newsletters
health - Fitness, wellness, medical
utilities - Cloud storage, domains, hosting
education - Courses, learning platforms
other - Anything else

Status Values

























StatusDescriptionactiveCurrently being billedpausedTemporarily suspended (not billing)cancelledNo longer activetrialFree trial period
Example
---
uid: 01JFXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
date: 2025-12-20
user: tomboo
type: subscription
title: Netflix
provider: Netflix Inc
amount: 15.99
currency: USD
frequency: monthly
billing-day: 15
next-billing: 2025-01-15
category: entertainment
status: active
payment-method: visa-1234
auto-renew: true
started-at: 2023-01-15
cancellation-url: netflix.com/cancel
tags: [streaming, video, family]
created-at: 2025-12-20T10:00:00-08:00
---
 
# Netflix
 
Premium streaming subscription with 4K support.
 
## Notes
 
- Shared with family (5 profiles)
- Premium tier for simultaneous streams
- Annual review: worth keeping for original content
Workflows
Adding a new subscription

Tell Claude about the subscription (name, cost, frequency, category)
Claude creates the file with ULID and calculated next-billing date
Subscription appears in views immediately

Monthly review

Open “Active Only” view grouped by category
Review each category’s total spend
Identify subscriptions to cancel or downgrade
Update status for any changes

Before renewal

Open “Upcoming Renewals” view
Review subscriptions billing in next 30 days
Decide to keep, cancel, or pause each one
Take action before billing date

Cancelling a subscription

Use the cancellation-url to cancel with provider
Update status to cancelled
Set cancelled-at date
Subscription moves to Cancelled view

Calculating Spend
To calculate monthly/yearly spend, Claude can sum amounts by frequency:

Monthly items: Use amount directly
Yearly items: Divide amount by 12 for monthly equivalent
Quarterly items: Divide amount by 3 for monthly equivalent
Weekly items: Multiply amount by 4.33 for monthly equivalent

Best Practices

Keep next-billing current - Update after each billing cycle
Use consistent payment-method names - Makes auditing easier
Add cancellation URLs - Makes cancelling frictionless
Review monthly - Prevent subscription creep
Track trials - Set status to trial with next-billing as trial end date

Troubleshooting
Subscription not appearing in views

Check that file is in _database/database-core/subscriptions-table/
Verify type: subscription in frontmatter
Reload the Base view in Obsidian

Incorrect next-billing date

Claude calculates based on frequency and billing-day
Manually update if billing cycle is irregular
Use file.mtime in Bases views to see when last updated

Category not matching

Use exact category values from the list above
Categories are kebab-case (e.g., health not Health)

Related

Subscriptions View
Dashboard
Template
Schema Definition

components/youtube/README.title: README
components/youtube/README.content:
YouTube App
Intentional YouTube queue management with priority-based viewing and knowledge capture.
Purpose
The YouTube app transforms reactive YouTube browsing into deliberate content consumption. Instead of algorithm-driven recommendations, maintain a prioritized queue of videos aligned with your learning goals and interests.
Key benefits:

Priority-based queue - Always know what to watch next
Categorized content - Organize by learning, entertainment, research
Knowledge capture - Take notes and rate watched content
Framework integration - Fits existing Personal OS workflows

Quick Start
Adding videos to the queue
Ask Claude to add a video using natural language:
add youtube youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ @learning high
queue video youtube.com/watch @entertainment
add to youtube queue youtu.be/xyz789 @tutorial p1

Supported parameters:

URL (required) - YouTube video URL
Category via @ prefix - learning, entertainment, research, tutorial, news, music, podcast, other
Priority - high/p1, medium/p2, low/p3, critical/p0
Tags via # prefix - any custom tags

Viewing the queue
Open components/youtube/youtube-base.base in Obsidian to see:

Watch Next - Queued items sorted by priority
By Category - Items grouped by content type
Currently Watching - Videos in progress
Watched - Completed with notes and ratings
All Items - Complete list with filtering

File Structure
components/youtube/
├── README.md                    # This file
├── youtube-dashboard.md         # Landing page
├── youtube-base.base            # Bases views
└── manifest.json

_database/database-core/youtube-table/    # Queue item files (ULID filenames)
_database/content-storage/youtube/        # Content files (video-id filenames)

Property Schema
Required Properties








































PropertyTypeDescriptiontypestringAlways “youtube”userstringOwner (tomboo)titlestringVideo titlecreated-atdatetimeWhen added to queueurlstringYouTube video URLvideo-idstring11-character YouTube video ID
Standard Properties






























PropertyTypeDescriptionstatusenumqueued, watching, watched, abandonedpriorityinteger0 (critical) to 3 (low)categoryenumContent category (see below)tagslistCustom tags
Optional Properties













































PropertyTypeDescriptionchannelstringChannel namedurationdurationVideo length (ISO 8601, e.g., PT15M30S)watched-atdatetimeWhen video was watchedratingintegerPersonal rating 1-5descriptionstringBrief description of video contentsynopsisstringDetailed summary or key points from the videocontent-filewikilinkLink to content storage file
Categories

learning - Educational content, courses, explanations
entertainment - Fun, relaxation, leisure viewing
research - Deep dives, investigations, analysis
tutorial - How-to guides, step-by-step instructions
news - Current events, updates, announcements
music - Music videos, performances, playlists
podcast - Long-form discussions, interviews
other - Anything else

Status Values

























StatusDescriptionqueuedIn watch list, not startedwatchingCurrently in progresswatchedCompleted viewingabandonedStarted but won’t finish
Example
---
type: youtube
user: tomboo
title: "How to Build a Second Brain"
created-at: 2026-01-15T10:00:00-08:00
status: queued
priority: 1
url: youtube.com/watch
video-id: dQw4w9WgXcQ
channel: Tiago Forte
duration: PT45M30S
category: learning
tags: [productivity, note-taking, pkm]
---
 
# How to Build a Second Brain
 
Tiago Forte explains the PARA method and building a second brain system.
 
## Notes
 
(Notes added while watching)
 
## Takeaways
 
(Key insights after watching)
Workflows
Adding a new video

Share URL from YouTube to Claude with category and priority
Claude extracts video-id, creates file with ULID filename
Optionally add title, channel, duration manually (Phase 1) or auto-fetch (Phase 3)
Video appears in “Watch Next” view

Watching a video

Open “Watch Next” view, pick highest priority item
Change status to watching
Watch video, add notes in the file
Change status to watched, optionally add rating
Video moves to “Watched” view

Reviewing watched content

Open “Watched” view
Review notes and ratings
Search for insights across watched videos
Link to other notes or projects as needed

URL Parsing
Claude extracts the video-id from various YouTube URL formats:

youtube.com/watch
www.youtube.com/watch
youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ
youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ

The video-id is always 11 characters: dQw4w9WgXcQ
Content Storage (Phase 2)
Content files store fetched metadata, transcripts, and chapters separately from queue items.
Directory Structure
_database/content-storage/youtube/
└── {video-id}.md    # e.g., 6qsPHOn8Rqs.md

Content File Properties

































































PropertyTypeDescriptiontypestringAlways “youtube-content”content-idstringYouTube video IDurlstringVideo URLfetched-atdatetimeWhen content was fetchedtitlestringVideo titlechannelstringChannel namechannel-urlstringChannel URLdurationdurationVideo lengthupload-datedateWhen uploadedview-countintegerViews at fetch timethumbnailstringThumbnail URL
Content File Body

Description - Video description from YouTube
Chapters - Timestamp markers (if available)
Transcript - Full text (use --transcript flag)

Linking Queue Items to Content
Add a content-file property to queue items:
content-file: "[[../../content-storage/youtube/6qsPHOn8Rqs]]"
Automated Fetching (Phase 3)
The youtube_fetcher.py script uses yt-dlp to fetch video metadata automatically.
Requirements

yt-dlp installed (brew install yt-dlp)

Usage
Fetch metadata as JSON:
python3 _framework/lib/youtube_fetcher.py <url_or_video_id> --json
Create content file:
python3 _framework/lib/youtube_fetcher.py <url_or_video_id>
Fetch with transcript (slower):
python3 _framework/lib/youtube_fetcher.py <url_or_video_id> --transcript
What Gets Fetched

Title, channel, channel URL
Duration (ISO 8601 format)
Upload date, view count
Thumbnail URL
Description
Chapters (if available)
Transcript (optional, requires --transcript flag)

Example
# Fetch metadata only
python3 _framework/lib/youtube_fetcher.py youtu.be/6qsPHOn8Rqs --json
 
# Create content file
python3 _framework/lib/youtube_fetcher.py 6qsPHOn8Rqs
# Creates: _database/content-storage/youtube/6qsPHOn8Rqs.md
Enhanced Workflows (Phase 4)
Quick Add Slash Command
Use /youtube-add to add videos with auto-fetched metadata:
/youtube-add <url> [@category] [priority] [#tags...]

Examples:
/youtube-add youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ
/youtube-add youtube.com/watch @learning high
/youtube-add youtu.be/xyz789 @tutorial p1 #python

Health Check
Check for orphaned content files and missing links:
python3 _framework/lib/youtube_fetcher.py --health
Checks:

Orphaned content files (content without queue item)
Missing content files (queue item without content)
Unlinked queue items (missing content-file property)

Open components/youtube/youtube-dashboard.md for:

Quick action commands
View descriptions
Workflow guide
Category reference

home.title: Vault Dashboard
home.content:
vault-personal-tom - Dashboard
Project: Personal Operating System v1.0
Type: Knowledge management, task tracking, and life organization

Your central hub for managing life priorities, tracking progress, and maintaining focus.


Quick Actions
Session Workflow
Start, checkpoint, and end work sessions with automatic note-taking:

/session-start - Begin new session (git sync, context check, recent activity)
/session-commit - Create checkpoint commit (~15-30 min intervals)
/session-end - Conclude session (auto-generate notes, health check, final commit)

Utilities

/context-status - Monitor context usage (color-coded thresholds)
/health-check - Validate vault health (schema, structure, naming)
/session-snapshot - Manual context consolidation with full transparency

Quick Capture

Notes - create note about [topic] (drafts for later triage)
Backlog - create backlog item to [description] (actionable items)

Current Session: No active session
See CLAUDE.md for detailed workflow documentation.

Database Apps
Your vault includes 5 active database apps powered by the Personal Operating System framework. Each app provides structured views for managing different aspects of your life and work.









































AppDescriptionData SourceStatusSessionsWork session tracking with Claude Code_database/database-core/sessions-table/ActiveProject ManagementUnified Areas → Projects → Tasks → Backlog (Things 3 inspired)_database/database-core/areas-table/, _database/database-core/projects-table/, _database/database-core/tasks-table/, _database/database-core/backlog-table/ActiveSubscriptionsRecurring payment tracking and cost visibility_database/database-core/subscriptions-table/ActiveNotesCasual notes, topical knowledge, personal insights_database/database-core/notes-table/ActiveApps RegistryMeta-tracking of framework apps_database/database-core/apps-table/Active
Quick Start:

Active tasks: Open Project Management → Tasks view → Today
High-priority backlog: Open Project Management → Backlog view
Recent sessions: See Recent Activity section below
Browse notes: Open Notes → All Notes view
Review subscriptions: Open Subscriptions → Active view

See individual app README files for view descriptions and usage guides.

Recent Activity
Recent Sessions
Last 5 work sessions (see all sessions):
dashboard-sessions.base
High-Priority Backlog
Top priority items requiring attention (see all backlog):
backlog-dashboard.base
Active Tasks
Current tasks sorted by priority (see all tasks):
tasks-dashboard.base
Recent Commits
# Run this to see recent commits:
git log --oneline -10
Or view commit history: Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P → “Git: View History”

Vault Metrics
Content Inventory


















































CategoryCountSourceWork Sessions36_database/database-core/sessions-table/Backlog Items50_database/database-core/backlog-table/Active Tasks84_database/database-core/tasks-table/Projects4_database/database-core/projects-table/Areas5_database/database-core/areas-table/Subscriptions6_database/database-core/subscriptions-table/Notes4_database/database-core/notes-table/Registered Apps6_database/database-core/apps-table/
Framework Health
Property Standards: ✓ Documented in Property Standards
Last health check: Run /health-check to verify
Status: ✓ Framework v2.1 operational
Run /health-check before major commits to validate:

Directory structure
Property schemas (frontmatter compliance)
Kebab-case naming conventions
ULID uniqueness and format
Wiki-link integrity (thorough mode)


Navigation
Key Directories

components/ - Database application views and documentation
_database/database-core/ - Database tables (sessions, backlog, tasks, projects, areas, subscriptions, notes, apps)
_database/database-docs/ - Framework documentation and schemas
lib/ - Python tooling (NLP parser, template engine, validators, link manager)
templates/ - File templates for content creation
tests/ - Testing infrastructure (pytest)
.claude/commands/ - Slash commands for session workflow

Documentation

CLAUDE - Complete AI workflow guide
Property Standards - Comprehensive property schema reference
Development Standards - Naming conventions and app pattern
AI Guidelines - AI responsibilities and workflows
Apps Registry - Registry of all apps

App READMEs

Sessions App - Session tracking
Project Management App - Unified Areas → Projects → Tasks → Backlog
Subscriptions App - Recurring payments
Notes App - Casual notes and knowledge
Apps Registry - Meta-app tracking

Tooling Documentation

NLP Parser - Natural language parsing for item creation
Template Engine - Variable substitution system
Link Manager - UID registry and relationship management

Templates
Create new content with standardized properties:

Backlog: backlog-template
Task: task-template
Project: project-template
Session: session-template
Subscription: subscription-template
Note: note-template
Daily Note: daily-note-template


Natural Language Creation
Use natural language to create backlog items and tasks:
Examples:
create backlog item to research Obsidian API tomorrow @learning #technical high 2h

create task to design mockup for Website Redesign due Friday p1

The NLP parser automatically extracts:

Dates (tomorrow, next week, Jan 15)
Priorities (high → p1, critical → p0)
Estimates (2h → P2H, 30m → PT30M)
Categories (@learning, @health-fitness)
Tags (#technical, urgent)

See NLP Parser for complete documentation.

Getting Started
First time here?

Run /session-start to begin your work session
Review CLAUDE for framework overview
Check Project Management to see what’s pending
Explore Property Standards to understand the schema
When finished, run /session-end to save session notes and commit changes

Daily workflow:

/session-start - Sync and review recent activity
Check this dashboard for high-priority items
Work on tasks, capture ideas to backlog
/session-commit periodically (~15-30 min intervals)
/session-end - Generate notes, health check, commit

Weekly maintenance:

Run /health-check to validate vault integrity
Review backlog → triage by priority, cancel irrelevant items
Review subscriptions → check upcoming renewals
Review areas/projects → update status, close completed items

Last Updated: 2025-12-25
Maintained By: Claude Code
